summary: Steel fire tower on Maple Mountain in Lady Evelyn-Smoothwater Provincial Park, 30 m (100 ft) tall, reached by a 3.2 km trail; build date not found.

facts.design: Steel tower with a square cupola

access.note: A 3.2 km trail within Lady Evelyn-Smoothwater Provincial Park leads to the tower. Sources call it abandoned and none says it is safe or permitted to climb.

visit.trail_note: A 3.2 km trail leads to the tower; the most popular approach is by canoe or float plane.

events.note: Shown on Gogama topographic map 41P, 3rd edition, per a Firelookout.ca photo credit
Proposed as a repeater station; not carried out (Firelookout.ca photo caption)

North Bay Fire #72, lightning-caused, grew to 27,285 ha; the marker says an aircraft detected the fire while it was flying to another fire near Lady Evelyn-Smoothwater Provincial Park, and that the tower stood as it burned

notes_for_editor: 'Rorke' is in the record name and the Firelookout.ca title and slug. No source read explains it, and a web search turned up nothing, so the story does not use the name. Build date unknown: Firelookout.ca gives Year Built N/A, and the Ontario tower layer (OBJECTID 2886, data/raw/ontario_lio/fire_towers.geojson) has no construction date or name. The 30 m height is from Wikipedia and matches the OSM value in the record. The builders from Bear Island and the 1985 repeater proposal come from one Firelookout.ca photo caption (credits Jeff Gilbert and Robert Eno), not confirmed elsewhere; the story says so in its wording. The caption says 'natives' without naming gender, so the story says 'two people'. The 2018 fire details come from an Ignace roadside marker, which uses emotive wording about the tower; the story keeps only the facts and the marker's own claim about the tower. The marker does not say where the detected fire was: it says the aircraft was enroute to another fire near the Temiskaming Shores, Lady Evelyn-Smoothwater Provincial Park, so the story says only that. The marker also calls the trail popular for 'hiking, climbing and mountaineering', which the story does not repeat. Access 'public' is inferred from the park and trail, not from a statement about the tower. The Ontario tower layer point matches the record coordinates. Record verification was 'unverified'; nothing here changes its coordinates or status. Fact-check 2026-10-20 corrected the 2018 event note, which earlier said the fire grew 'in the park area'; the marker does not say that.
